Operational motivation 
During maintenance, one member of a storage cluster may be unavailable for several hours. Bringing
that member back into service puts extra traffic on the same machines that serve user requests. This
design memo describes a recovery path for such cases. Its intended audience is a storage operator
choosing how to reintroduce a stale machine during an otherwise busy period.

Lag-Aware Snapshots for Replicated Key-Value Stores

Scope
A replicated key-value store must sometimes move a large snapshot while foreground requests continue. We consider followers that have fallen far enough behind for log replay to compete with ordinary traffic. The proposal targets a leader with several followers and assumes monotonically numbered log entries. It separates the question of which version to copy from the question of how fast the transfer should proceed.

entries. It separates the question of which version to copy from the question of how fast the transfer should proceed.

Snapshot boundary
The leader seals a snapshot at a committed log index and advertises that index before sending any data. A follower stages the incoming key ranges in a separate directory. It installs the directory only after checking the manifest and the digest of every range. Log entries above the sealed index remain in a replay queue.

checking the manifest and the digest of every range. Log entries above the sealed index remain in a replay queue. This boundary prevents a transfer from combining keys that were observed at different points in the update history.

Transfer scheduling
A token bucket at the sender caps the amount of snapshot data emitted during each scheduling interval. Foreground reads may borrow bandwidth from an idle snapshot stream.

the amount of snapshot data emitted during each scheduling interval. Foreground reads may borrow bandwidth from an idle snapshot stream. The bucket is replenished from a rolling estimate of spare link capacity, using measurements taken before the next group of ranges is issued. A paused transfer keeps its verified ranges so that resumption begins with the earliest unchecked range.

Tracking Prediction Quality While
Confirmation Arrives Late 
Design overview 
Consider a diagnostic service for factory sensors whose outputs are reviewed by a separate
maintenance desk. A defect can be verified well after the alarm appears. The question is how to give an
engineer a credible picture of the predictor while the desk is still working through its open tickets. The
design treats the reporting date and the actual time of the alarm as distinct facts.

design treats the reporting date and the actual time of the alarm as distinct facts. 
When to trust a score 
Straightforward faults tend to be settled ahead of ambiguous ones. As a result, the subset closed early
can make the system look more accurate than it will once the difficult files have been examined. For
each class of machine, contrast promptly closed tickets with ones that stayed open longer.

difficult files have been examined. For
each class of machine, contrast promptly closed tickets with ones that stayed open longer. If they
behave differently, wait for the pending tickets before saying that one predictor performs better than
another. 
Presentation notes 
The diagnostic console would reserve a panel for incoming alarms and another for records requiring
additional context. The reporting page would display a small legend that explains which estimates are
still being updated.

Delayed Labels in a Streaming Fault Classifier

Problem setting
A monitoring model categorizes telemetry bursts from industrial equipment. Human reviewers may confirm an incident days after the corresponding burst. Confirmation lag varies by maintenance shift and by the kind of event. The proposed study concerns the reliability of model evaluation during such gaps. Each prediction is archived with its probability vector, emission time, model version, and an identifier that can be joined to a later investigation record.

with its probability vector, emission time, model version, and an identifier that can be joined to a later investigation record.

Evaluation cohorts
Assign each observation to an evaluation cohort using the time of inference. The arrival of an adjudication is only a signal to update the older cohort. It never moves the observation into a more recent bucket. Otherwise a day with a backlog clearance may look unusually difficult even though its predictions were ordinary.

more recent bucket. Otherwise a day with a backlog clearance may look unusually difficult even though its predictions were ordinary. A report includes the fraction of cases already adjudicated, and readers can distinguish provisional scores from mature ones.

Reference schedule
We propose a weekly frozen comparator and a second model that updates on a fixed schedule. Both predictors receive the same feature snapshots and produce output before any adjudication is available.

updates on a fixed schedule. Both predictors receive the same feature snapshots and produce output before any adjudication is available. Review staff should not see which system supplied a particular estimate. The protocol records the ages of unresolved incidents and groups evaluation views by equipment category to expose delays that affect only one part of the installation.

Correction records
Store per-event contributions to the evaluation counters until adjudications are stable.

affect only one part of the installation.

Correction records
Store per-event contributions to the evaluation counters until adjudications are stable. When a reviewer replaces an earlier label, remove the contribution computed from the superseded value and add one computed from the revised value. The correction must update the original aggregate rather than append a second case. This design keeps repeated amendments from inflating the sample size and lets investigators reconstruct the value published at any checkpoint.

This design keeps repeated amendments from inflating the sample size and lets investigators reconstruct the value published at any checkpoint.

Shift analysis
A deployment may have quiet weekends and unusually concentrated weekday inspections. The proposed replay uses intact weekly blocks so that this pattern remains visible. Stratifying randomly by individual record would spread weekend bursts across the whole calendar and hide the periods in which feedback is sparse. We would inspect differences across shifts before combining the results.

calendar and hide the periods in which feedback is sparse. We would inspect differences across shifts before combining the results. The design specifies an analysis plan and supplies no measured outcome.

Bias from fast decisions
Initial confirmations often overrepresent incidents with obvious symptoms because they are quicker for reviewers to resolve. The current precision estimate can therefore appear better than the final estimate. Compare prompt and delayed decisions within each equipment family before trusting the early curve.

SYNTHETIC CS RESEARCH NOTE 
Dictionary Reuse in a Columnar Product
Catalog 
Catalog workload 
A retailer keeps one analytical column for each product attribute. Material names, package
descriptions, and manufacturing regions repeat across many rows, although the relative frequency of
those strings changes with the season. The storage proposal groups nearby rows into stripes and
encodes recurring values with small integers. Its goal is to reduce the bytes examined by scans that
filter products by a common attribute.

with small integers. Its goal is to reduce the bytes examined by scans that
filter products by a common attribute. 
Shared string tables 
A stripe dictionary is small when many rows contain the same names. Two adjacent stripes may
nevertheless carry almost identical dictionaries, wasting storage on duplicate strings. The writer can
build a shared table for a run of stripes when the union of their values stays modest.

The writer can
build a shared table for a run of stripes when the union of their values stays modest. Each stripe stores
its own compact sequence of indexes while reading spellings from the shared table. 
Deciding where to split 
The compactor estimates the number of bits needed for an index before adding another stripe to a
group. If the combined vocabulary crosses a power of two, every encoded index may become wider.

another stripe to a
group. If the combined vocabulary crosses a power of two, every encoded index may become wider.
The storage gain from deleting duplicate names must cover this extra cost. The planner also limits
group size to keep the working set small when a query touches only one range of rows.

Filtering without materialization 
A predicate against a literal value first looks up the corresponding integer in the dictionary. If the value
is absent, the executor can skip all associated rows. When the value exists, the executor compares
packed indexes and decodes full strings only for rows selected for output.

in alphabetic order use an ordering map alongside the dictionary.

The evaluation would synthesize catalogs with frequent attributes, changing brand distributions, and
sparse optional fields. It would measure encoded size, dictionary build time, and scan throughput under
selective and nonselective filters.

Capability Rotation for Guest Network Gateways

Threat model
A municipal wireless gateway offers short guest sessions to devices that have no persistent identity. An attacker who captures a bearer capability might replay it from a different radio segment. The proposed protocol assumes encrypted management traffic and untrusted client networks. It does not try to identify a person or link visits across locations.

encrypted management traffic and untrusted client networks. It does not try to identify a person or link visits across locations. Its main objective is to confine the effect of a stolen capability to a small region and time interval.

Capability format
Each grant carries an audience describing the access zone, an expiry measured against the gateway clock, and an unpredictable nonce. The issuing service signs the fields as a single authenticated message.

measured against the gateway clock, and an unpredictable nonce. The issuing service signs the fields as a single authenticated message. A gateway must reject a grant when the audience does not describe its own zone, even when the signature is valid. Admission packets also include a challenge response bound to the association that originally requested the grant.

Rotation policy
Verification keys change on a fixed schedule, with a short overlap to handle clocks that differ slightly.

grant.

Rotation policy
Verification keys change on a fixed schedule, with a short overlap to handle clocks that differ slightly. A revoked signing key bypasses the normal overlap window. Radios receive the revocation status through an authenticated management channel. When a device moves into a neighboring zone it requests a new grant. Handing its existing grant to the next gateway would extend the usefulness of a stolen message.

requests a new grant. Handing its existing grant to the next gateway would extend the usefulness of a stolen message.

Replay accounting
Gateways retain recently consumed nonces for the validity period of the grants. A bounded table records the zone and the expiry associated with each entry. The table drops expired nonces during a periodic maintenance pass. If available space runs low, the admission path temporarily slows new associations to preserve the validity of replay checks for already issued grants.

runs low, the admission path temporarily slows new associations to preserve the validity of replay checks for already issued grants.

Assessment plan
The proposed exercise places one radio on a congested channel and another on a quiet channel. A traffic generator submits stale messages, duplicate challenges, and grants intended for a different zone. The observer records which messages reach the admission stage and which are refused earlier.

grants intended for a different zone. The observer records which messages reach the admission stage and which are refused earlier. This synthetic plan reports no attack success rate and makes no claim about deployed networks.
